summary: Configured node1 as a persistent internal DNS resolver and node2 to use it. Resolution, forwarding, firewall restrictions, SELinux enforcement, and reboot persistence were verified on both nodes.
actions_performed: Installed and configured dnsmasq on node1 for inventory-api.internal → 10.100.85.11.
Restricted DNS access through firewalld to node2 (10.100.85.11/32).
Configured node2’s persistent NetworkManager profile to use node1 (10.100.85.10) and ignore DHCP DNS.
Added network-online startup ordering after the first node1 reboot exposed a DHCP-address race.
Removed incompatible optional bind-utils packages and cleaned package caches.
Restarted nodes sequentially and verified changed boot identities and complete recovery.

evidence.requirement: Node1 provides the requested internal DNS record
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is enabled, active, listening on TCP/UDP 10.100.85.10:53, and returns 10.100.85.11 for inventory-api.internal.

evidence.requirement: Node2 persistently uses node1 for DNS
evidence.summary: NetworkManager and resolv.conf use 10.100.85.10; both direct DNS and libc resolution succeed.
SELinux remains enforcing and firewalld permits DNS only from node2’s IPv4 /32.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel were preserved
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64.
Healthy baseline boot ID 8a6993cc…; reboot acknowledged; new boot ID 86d05c0b…; system, DNS service, listeners, firewall, internal resolution, and forwarding recovered.
Healthy baseline boot ID 5eed1606…; reboot acknowledged and disconnect observed; new boot ID 5329f2da…; NetworkManager, address, DNS profile, internal resolution, and public forwarding recovered.
